name: Partial-Cube and Interval-Gap Equivalence
hypotheses: Finite nonempty binary family with its one-inclusion graph.
statement: Isometry of the one-inclusion graph in the ambient cube is equivalent to the absence of an empty interval between concepts at Hamming distance greater than one.
proof: If the embedding is isometric, a geodesic supplies an intermediate concept in every nontrivial interval. Conversely, when $g(C)=0$, every pair at distance greater than one has an intermediate concept in its interval; induction on Hamming distance concatenates geodesics through such concepts and proves isometry.
